chapter: Benny Carter, saxophones and Coleman Hawkins's last years
title: Why Hawkins broke down and his eating
summary: Dance thinks the Swiss girlfriend's departure broke him; they recall his weakness and former hearty appetite.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I think, you know, he did have this Swiss first girl, and she left him.
Oh.
And I think that did sort of break him up.
Maybe it could. Maybe it did. Maybe there was something behind that.
(Simultaneous remarks)
But I mean I think it was really
his fault. He was getting pretty bad, you know, --
Yes, I see.
-- drinking and --
(Simultaneous remarks)
But I think that sort of broke him up more than people realize.
Well, that's what this fellow was telling me. I couldn't believe it.
Yeah.
Maybe there was some truth to it.

I think so because, as long as, you know, she was in the apartment and everything, he could go home and there was somebody there, but then after she left, he'd still got this apartment, and I guess he felt lonely, you know?
Yeah, most -- most likely.

Yeah. But I mean by this time he was -- you know, he was failing. He was -- as Charlie said, he -- you know, he'd got this awful long beard and lost so much weight, and he was weak. He was really very weak.
Had to be.
He couldn't eat, you know. He tried to eat, but it wouldn't --
(Unintelligible). He used to be a hearty eater too.

Huh. But the last, you know, he didn't really -- well, I know, oh, a long time before he died, he -- I didn't know whether his teeth had got bad or -- but he couldn't -- he was sort of, you know, masticating everything --
(Simultaneous remarks)
-- chewing away as though it was a real chore.
Yes, it was.
He was in --
Pine guy too.
(Simultaneous remarks)
-- with Chinese food.
Something to digest quick. That's what it was.
Yeah, you know --
(Simultaneous remarks)
We used to go sometimes -- he loved these steaks, mushrooms, steaks, salad, because he was a heavy -- he was a very good, hearty eater, very good, hearty eater.
In those days I suppose people used to believe it --
(Laughter)
-- if they could afford it. Now, everybody's thinking, I mustn't eat that and (unintelligible).
